dialogue.text: The world's worst civilian nuclear disaster took place when a reactor exploded.
dialogue.zh: 世界上最嚴重的民用核災難發生在一座反應爐爆炸時。
dialogue.ja: 世界最悪の民間用原子力災害は、原子炉が爆発したときに起こりました。
dialogue.local: The world's worst civilian nuclear disaster took place when a reactor exploded.
dialogue.en: The world's worst civilian nuclear disaster took place when a reactor exploded.

dialogue.text: At the Chernobyl power plant in Ukraine, then part of the Soviet Union, present-day Belarus
dialogue.zh: 在當時屬於蘇聯的烏克蘭切爾諾貝利核電廠，現今的白俄羅斯
dialogue.ja: 当時ソ連の一部だったウクライナのチェルノブイリ発電所で、現在のベラルーシは
dialogue.local: At the Chernobyl power plant in Ukraine, then part of the Soviet Union, present-day Belarus
dialogue.en: At the Chernobyl power plant in Ukraine, then part of the Soviet Union, present-day Belarus

dialogue.text: received 60 percent of the initial fallout.
dialogue.zh: 接收了60%的初期放射性落塵。
dialogue.ja: 初期の放射性降下物の60％を受け取りました。
dialogue.local: received 60 percent of the initial fallout.
dialogue.en: received 60 percent of the initial fallout.

dialogue.text: The radioactive cloud spread further to cover most of Europe.
dialogue.zh: 放射性雲進一步擴散，覆蓋了大部分歐洲。
dialogue.ja: 放射性の雲はさらに広がり、ヨーロッパの大部分を覆いました。
dialogue.local: The radioactive cloud spread further to cover most of Europe.
dialogue.en: The radioactive cloud spread further to cover most of Europe.

dialogue.text: The Chernobyl nuclear power plant was one of the Soviet Union's most advanced facilities.
dialogue.zh: 切爾諾貝利核電廠是蘇聯最先進的設施之一。
dialogue.ja: チェルノブイリ原子力発電所は、ソ連で最も先進的な施設の一つでした。
dialogue.local: The Chernobyl nuclear power plant was one of the Soviet Union's most advanced facilities.
dialogue.en: The Chernobyl nuclear power plant was one of the Soviet Union's most advanced facilities.

dialogue.text: The first two reactors became operational in the late 1970s.
dialogue.zh: 前兩座反應爐於1970年代末開始運作。
dialogue.ja: 最初の2基の原子炉は1970年代後半に稼働を開始しました。
dialogue.local: The first two reactors became operational in the late 1970s.
dialogue.en: The first two reactors became operational in the late 1970s.

dialogue.text: The fourth reactor was the newest, going online in 1983.
dialogue.zh: 第四號反應爐是最新的，於1983年投入運行。
dialogue.ja: 4号炉は最新で、1983年に稼働を開始しました。
dialogue.local: The fourth reactor was the newest, going online in 1983.
dialogue.en: The fourth reactor was the newest, going online in 1983.

dialogue.text: On April 26, 1986, technicians prepared to test the backup cooling system in reactor
dialogue.zh: 1986年4月26日，技術人員準備測試第四號反應爐的備用冷卻系統，
dialogue.ja: 1986年4月26日、技術者たちは4号炉のバックアップ冷却システムのテストを準備しました。
dialogue.local: On April 26, 1986, technicians prepared to test the backup cooling system in reactor
dialogue.en: On April 26, 1986, technicians prepared to test the backup cooling system in reactor

dialogue.text: number four, but the routine safety drill went horribly wrong.
dialogue.zh: 但這次例行的安全演習出了嚴重問題。
dialogue.ja: しかし、通常の安全訓練がひどく失敗しました。
dialogue.local: number four, but the routine safety drill went horribly wrong.
dialogue.en: number four, but the routine safety drill went horribly wrong.

dialogue.text: A nuclear reactor is like a giant steam engine.
dialogue.zh: 核反應爐就像一台巨大的蒸汽機。
dialogue.ja: 原子炉は巨大な蒸気機関のようなものです。
dialogue.local: A nuclear reactor is like a giant steam engine.
dialogue.en: A nuclear reactor is like a giant steam engine.

dialogue.text: Uranium fuel rods react to produce a massive amount of heat.
dialogue.zh: 鈾燃料棒反應產生大量熱能。
dialogue.ja: ウラン燃料棒が反応して大量の熱を生み出します。
dialogue.local: Uranium fuel rods react to produce a massive amount of heat.
dialogue.en: Uranium fuel rods react to produce a massive amount of heat.

dialogue.text: That converts water into steam, which drives huge turbines to generate electricity.
dialogue.zh: 這些熱能將水轉化為蒸汽，推動大型渦輪機發電。
dialogue.ja: その熱で水が蒸気に変わり、大きなタービンを回して電気を作ります。
dialogue.local: That converts water into steam, which drives huge turbines to generate electricity.
dialogue.en: That converts water into steam, which drives huge turbines to generate electricity.

dialogue.text: Control rods are inserted in between the uranium to slow the reaction, and it's crucial for
dialogue.zh: 控制棒插入鈾棒之間以減緩反應，並且必須持續循環冷卻水以防止過熱。
dialogue.ja: 制御棒はウランの間に挿入されて反応を遅らせます。また、過熱を防ぐために冷却水を循環させることが重要です。
dialogue.local: Control rods are inserted in between the uranium to slow the reaction, and it's crucial for
dialogue.en: Control rods are inserted in between the uranium to slow the reaction, and it's crucial for

dialogue.text: cooling water to be pumped around the core to prevent overheating.
dialogue.zh: 冷卻水必須在核心周圍循環以防止過熱。
dialogue.ja: 冷却水が炉心の周りを循環して過熱を防ぐことが不可欠です。
dialogue.local: cooling water to be pumped around the core to prevent overheating.
dialogue.en: cooling water to be pumped around the core to prevent overheating.

dialogue.text: But as the test began, almost all of the control rods were removed, and technicians
dialogue.zh: 但測試開始時，幾乎所有控制棒都被拔出，技術人員
dialogue.ja: しかし、テストが始まるとほとんど全ての制御棒が抜かれ、技術者たちは
dialogue.local: But as the test began, almost all of the control rods were removed, and technicians
dialogue.en: But as the test began, almost all of the control rods were removed, and technicians

dialogue.text: lost control with a flow of cooling.
dialogue.zh: 失去了對冷卻水流的控制。
dialogue.ja: 冷却水の流れを制御できなくなりました。
dialogue.local: lost control with a flow of cooling.
dialogue.en: lost control with a flow of cooling.

dialogue.text: Temperatures soared, and extreme heat began to melt the core.
dialogue.zh: 溫度飆升，極端高溫開始融化反應爐核心。
dialogue.ja: 温度が急上昇し、極度の熱で炉心が溶け始めました。
dialogue.local: Temperatures soared, and extreme heat began to melt the core.
dialogue.en: Temperatures soared, and extreme heat began to melt the core.

dialogue.text: At 123 AM, reactor four exploded.
dialogue.zh: 凌晨1點23分，第四號反應爐爆炸了。
dialogue.ja: 午前1時23分に4号炉が爆発しました。
dialogue.local: At 123 AM, reactor four exploded.
dialogue.en: At 123 AM, reactor four exploded.

dialogue.text: It spewed eight tons of radioactive debris into the atmosphere.
dialogue.zh: 它向大氣中噴出八噸放射性碎片。
dialogue.ja: 8トンの放射性破片を大気中に撒き散らしました。
dialogue.local: It spewed eight tons of radioactive debris into the atmosphere.
dialogue.en: It spewed eight tons of radioactive debris into the atmosphere.

dialogue.text: 115,000 people were evacuated from a 30-kilometer zone around the plants.
dialogue.zh: 從核電廠周圍30公里範圍內疏散了115,000人。
dialogue.ja: 発電所周辺30キロメートルの区域から11万5千人が避難しました。
dialogue.local: 115,000 people were evacuated from a 30-kilometer zone around the plants.
dialogue.en: 115,000 people were evacuated from a 30-kilometer zone around the plants.

dialogue.text: The battle to put out the fires inside lasted for 15 days, more than a half a million
dialogue.zh: 撲滅內部火災的戰鬥持續了15天，超過50萬名軍事和民間人員被徵召來處理事故及其後果。
dialogue.ja: 内部の火災を消す戦いは15日間続き、50万人以上の軍人と民間人が事故とその後処理に動員されました。
dialogue.local: The battle to put out the fires inside lasted for 15 days, more than a half a million
dialogue.en: The battle to put out the fires inside lasted for 15 days, more than a half a million

dialogue.text: military and civilian personnel were drafted to deal with the accident and its aftermath.
dialogue.zh: 超過50萬名軍事和民間人員被徵召來處理事故及其後果。
dialogue.ja: 軍人と民間人合わせて50万人以上が事故とその後始末に動員されました。
dialogue.local: military and civilian personnel were drafted to deal with the accident and its aftermath.
dialogue.en: military and civilian personnel were drafted to deal with the accident and its aftermath.

dialogue.text: 31 of the initial firefighters and plant workers died within days from acute radiation
dialogue.zh: 最初的31名消防員和廠區工作人員在幾天內死於急性輻射病。
dialogue.ja: 最初の31人の消防士と工場労働者が数日以内に急性放射線障害で亡くなりました。
dialogue.local: 31 of the initial firefighters and plant workers died within days from acute radiation
dialogue.en: 31 of the initial firefighters and plant workers died within days from acute radiation

dialogue.text: sickness.
dialogue.zh: 輻射病。
dialogue.ja: 放射線障害です。
dialogue.local: sickness.
dialogue.en: sickness.

dialogue.text: The toxicity of the radioactive cloud was equivalent to 400 Hiroshima atomic bomb explosions.
dialogue.zh: 放射性雲的毒性相當於400顆廣島原子彈爆炸。
dialogue.ja: 放射性の雲の毒性は広島原爆400発分に相当しました。
dialogue.local: The toxicity of the radioactive cloud was equivalent to 400 Hiroshima atomic bomb explosions.
dialogue.en: The toxicity of the radioactive cloud was equivalent to 400 Hiroshima atomic bomb explosions.

dialogue.text: Crews hastily built a concrete sarcophagus to encase the entire reactor to prevent
dialogue.zh: 工作人員匆忙建造混凝土石棺包裹整個反應爐，以防止
dialogue.ja: 作業員たちは急いでコンクリートの石棺を建設し、原子炉全体を覆って
dialogue.local: Crews hastily built a concrete sarcophagus to encase the entire reactor to prevent
dialogue.en: Crews hastily built a concrete sarcophagus to encase the entire reactor to prevent

dialogue.text: more radiation from spreading.
dialogue.zh: 更多輻射擴散。
dialogue.ja: さらなる放射線の拡散を防ぎました。
dialogue.local: more radiation from spreading.
dialogue.en: more radiation from spreading.

dialogue.text: Inside the remained 200 tons of radioactive fuel.
dialogue.zh: 裡面還剩下200噸放射性燃料。
dialogue.ja: 内部には200トンの放射性燃料が残っていました。
dialogue.local: Inside the remained 200 tons of radioactive fuel.
dialogue.en: Inside the remained 200 tons of radioactive fuel.

dialogue.text: The remaining three reactors continued to operate due to energy shortages in Ukraine.
dialogue.zh: 由於烏克蘭能源短缺，剩餘的三座反應爐繼續運作。
dialogue.ja: ウクライナのエネルギー不足のため、残りの3基の原子炉は稼働を続けました。
dialogue.local: The remaining three reactors continued to operate due to energy shortages in Ukraine.
dialogue.en: The remaining three reactors continued to operate due to energy shortages in Ukraine.

dialogue.text: It wasn't until the year 2000 that the Chernobyl complex was completely shut down.
dialogue.zh: 直到2000年，切爾諾貝利核電廠才完全關閉。
dialogue.ja: チェルノブイリ複合施設が完全に閉鎖されたのは2000年になってからでした。
dialogue.local: It wasn't until the year 2000 that the Chernobyl complex was completely shut down.
dialogue.en: It wasn't until the year 2000 that the Chernobyl complex was completely shut down.

dialogue.text: With the concrete sarcophagus crumbling, the international community began to build a new confinement
dialogue.zh: 隨著混凝土石棺逐漸崩壞，國際社會開始建造新的圍封結構，
dialogue.ja: コンクリートの石棺が崩れ始めたため、国際社会は新しい閉鎖構造の建設を始めました。
dialogue.local: With the concrete sarcophagus crumbling, the international community began to build a new confinement
dialogue.en: With the concrete sarcophagus crumbling, the international community began to build a new confinement

dialogue.text: structure for reactor four.
dialogue.zh: 用於第四號反應爐的結構。
dialogue.ja: 4号炉のための構造物です。
dialogue.local: structure for reactor four.
dialogue.en: structure for reactor four.

dialogue.text: It stands 110 meters tall, higher than the Statue of Liberty, and it's wide enough to
dialogue.zh: 它高110米，比自由女神像還高，寬度足以
dialogue.ja: 高さ110メートルで、自由の女神像よりも高く、幅は
dialogue.local: It stands 110 meters tall, higher than the Statue of Liberty, and it's wide enough to
dialogue.en: It stands 110 meters tall, higher than the Statue of Liberty, and it's wide enough to

dialogue.text: fit a ship the size of the Titanic.
dialogue.zh: 容納一艘泰坦尼克號大小的船隻。
dialogue.ja: タイタニック号の大きさの船を収容できるほど広いです。
dialogue.local: fit a ship the size of the Titanic.
dialogue.en: fit a ship the size of the Titanic.

dialogue.text: At a projected cost of $3 billion, construction is scheduled for completion in 2017.
dialogue.zh: 預計耗資30億美元，建設計劃於2017年完成。
dialogue.ja: 建設費用は約30億ドルで、2017年の完成予定です。
dialogue.local: At a projected cost of $3 billion, construction is scheduled for completion in 2017.
dialogue.en: At a projected cost of $3 billion, construction is scheduled for completion in 2017.

dialogue.text: One of Chernobyl's iconic red and white chimneys will be dismantled, and the massive steel
dialogue.zh: 切爾諾貝利標誌性的紅白煙囪之一將被拆除，巨大的鋼製
dialogue.ja: チェルノブイリの象徴的な赤と白の煙突の一つが解体され、巨大な鉄製の
dialogue.local: One of Chernobyl's iconic red and white chimneys will be dismantled, and the massive steel
dialogue.en: One of Chernobyl's iconic red and white chimneys will be dismantled, and the massive steel

dialogue.text: dome will slide over reactor number four.
dialogue.zh: 圓頂將滑動覆蓋第四號反應爐。
dialogue.ja: ドームが4号炉の上にスライドして覆います。
dialogue.local: dome will slide over reactor number four.
dialogue.en: dome will slide over reactor number four.

dialogue.text: The confinement structure is expected to last for at least 100 years.
dialogue.zh: 這個圍封結構預計至少能持續100年。
dialogue.ja: この閉鎖構造は少なくとも100年間持つと予想されています。
dialogue.local: The confinement structure is expected to last for at least 100 years.
dialogue.en: The confinement structure is expected to last for at least 100 years.
